text:
arjun: Heads-up — ACME just pushed a hard ask to include their SSO and per-tenant analytics in the initial launch. They said "can't go live without SSO", but they only represent ~8% of early pilot revenue. We need a fast scope call.

maya: ack. do we have a clear cost/latency delta for adding SSO + analytics? rough numbers fine.

sam: SSO adds ~2 sprint of eng work (integration + e2e), analytics + dashboard another sprint. Risk: auth flows add infra surface area for Dedicated customers. Latency change minimal after caching.

jess: UX-wise we can scaffold a minimal SSO flow (social + SAML metadata upload) in 1 sprint but it won't cover advanced ACME edge cases.

arjun: proposal A = ship MVP (core inference routes, tenant routing, basic billing) by May 8. Defer full SSO + analytics to v1.

arjun: proposal B = include minimal SSO + basic per-tenant dashboard and push launch 2 weeks.

maya: Two quick constraints we should use as gates: 1) No-regressions on 99th latency for hosted API, 2) Basic SSO test matrix (SSO login, fallback) passes in staging. If either fails, fallback to proposal A.

sam: +1 on the gates. Also add an ops gate: runbook for SSO key rotation and monitoring in place.

jess: If we go B, design will ship a toned-down dashboard that hits the 'visibility' requirement without full query builder.

arjun: To make the decision faster: what's the customer tradeoff? ACME signs an LOI if SSO in launch window. If we defer, they may pilot but delay payment.

maya: Financially that matters, but we should quantify: estimated incremental ARR if ACME converted on launch: ~$45k ARR. Team cost to accelerate: ~3 engineer-sprints across two teams + design.

sam: engineering prefers A unless exec signals to prioritize ACME. Risk profile for B: higher operational support at launch, possible rollback complexity.

jess: design prefers B for customer confidence but won’t block A.

product-bot: ACME LOI doc: https://acme.example/loi — noted in board. :memo:

arjun: Ok quick decision heuristic I want to use (vote):
- If incremental ARR > cost_threshold (2 months runway cost) -> commit to B.
- Else -> A with clear outreach plan + pilot checklist.

maya: Calculated ARR bump vs cost: borderline but slightly below our threshold unless we reassign one backend headcount for 3 weeks.

sam: Reassigning one backend lead for 3 weeks is doable if we pause non-critical infra work. That removes the schedule slip.

arjun: Action items: 
- @sam: map exact sprint tasks and dependency list by EOD today (1767009600).
- @jess: mock the minimal SSO + dashboard UI and share prototype by tomorrow noon.
- @maya: draft customer outreach script if we defer (explain pilot + timeline) and share with sales.
- @product-bot: create a short canary checklist and a rollback plan stub in the launch doc.

sam: got it. I'll post a breakdown.

jess: prototyping now. will post link.

maya: outreach draft ready for review in an hour.

product-bot: Canary checklist created at https://redwood.internal/launchs/1767009123/canary-checklist :white_check_mark:

arjun: Final note: We prefer to avoid a timeline reset but not at the cost of a poor first experience. Let's reconvene 48h or sooner if blockers. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: thanks — pinging infra to freeze non-critical infra merges for 3 weeks to free up bandwidth.

jess: sharing prototype: https://figma.com/proto/ssominimal (comments welcome) :eyes:

maya: leaving a +1 for B if we can confirm the reassign. Otherwise A.

arjun: agreed. closing for now — will update thread after sam posts the task breakdown.

sam: posted task list and ETA: https://redwood.internal/boards/issue/SSO-1767 — looks like 11 dev-days total; can hit B if we reassign.

arjun: thanks. tagging execs for awareness: @cto @ceo — recommend minor shuffle to hit B for ACME LOI.

product-bot: Exec notification sent to #exec-alerts.
